newsitem.title: SPAIN: Euro convergence progress is ambivalent - Issing.
newsitem.headline: Euro convergence progress is ambivalent - Issing.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Otmar Issing said on Thursday that reports from the European Commission and the European Monetary Institute showed that progress so far on convergence was ambivalent.
"In the light of these reports the findings on the progress on convergence made so far are ambivalent," said Issing in prepared text to be delivered to bankers in Pamplona.

"It is true that, on the one hand, inflation rates have been significantly reduced and that nominal long-term interest rates of most countries have converged distinctly as a result. On the other hand, consolidation of public finance is still largely unsatisfactory," Issing said.

Issing said almost every EU country significantly exceeded the qualifying thresholds of three percent of gross domestic product for the current budget deficit and of sixty percent for total government debt.
He said further improvement in public finance was key to the selection of candidates for the launch of Europe's single currency.
"The group of candidates selected for monetary union therefore, depends decisively on further consolidation in the area of public finance," Issing said.
He added that this explained why criticism of strict adherence to the budget criteria was getting louder.
"It is hardly surprising in such a situation that criticism of the sense and purpose of strictly adhering to the budget criteria is getting louder," Issing said.
He voiced severe criticism of budgetary "manipulation," but he did not name names.

"Dressing up the figures on budget deficits or government debt by imaginitive manipulation. Even if, in individual cases, this is compatible, in a formal sense, with the guidelines on the national accounts is certainly not consistent with the spirit of the relevant provisions in the Maastricht Treaty," Issing said.

If deficits for today or more precisely, for 1997, are shown to be lower than they really are and if this means an increase in the future in these deficits, "this will infringe the condition of sustainability of budget policy."
